quick: 20 g orally once daily (reduce to 10 g for loose stools)
Minimally absorbed; use if needed - data limited
Stool frequency/consistency, hydration, electrolytes if prolonged
summary: Lactitol (Pizensy) is an osmotic laxative sugar alcohol indicated for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults. The recommended dose is 20 grams orally once daily, preferably with meals, reduced to 10 grams for persistent loose stools. It is minimally absorbed and acts by drawing water into the intestine.
admin: Mix the measured dose (cap fills to 10 g; unit-dose packets contain 10 g each) into 4 to 8 ounces of water, juice or other beverage
Stir and drink; the powder dissolves readily
Take once daily, preferably with a meal
Administer other oral medications at least 2 hours before or 2 hours after lactitol
moa: Lactitol is a minimally absorbed disaccharide-analog sugar alcohol that exerts an osmotic effect in the gastrointestinal tract. It draws water into the small intestine and is fermented by colonic bacteria, increasing stool water content and intestinal motility to produce a laxative effect in the colon.

absolute: Known or suspected mechanical gastrointestinal obstruction
Hypersensitivity to lactitol or any component
relative: Galactosemia (lactitol is a galactose-glucitol; theoretical caution)

preg: Lactitol is minimally absorbed systemically; available data are insufficient to identify a drug-associated risk, and animal studies showed no adverse developmental effects. May be used in pregnancy when clinically indicated.
lact: Because lactitol is minimally absorbed systemically, clinically relevant exposure in breast milk and to the breastfed infant is unlikely. Use is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding.
renal: No dosage adjustment is needed; lactitol is minimally absorbed and not dependent on renal elimination. Monitor fluid/electrolyte status if diarrhea is significant.
hepatic: No specific dosage adjustment is required for hepatic impairment given minimal systemic absorption.

moderate: Oral medications - lactitol may reduce absorption; separate administration by at least 2 hours
minor: Other laxatives - additive effect, risk of diarrhea/dehydration
interactions.food: Take preferably with meals; food does not impair the laxative effect.
interactions.diagnostics: May raise blood creatine phosphokinase; significant diarrhea can alter electrolytes.

serious: Severe diarrhea with dehydration and electrolyte imbalance
emergency: Severe dehydration / electrolyte disturbance from prolonged diarrhea

monitoring: Serum electrolytes if prolonged or severe diarrhea
counsel: Dissolve the dose in 4-8 ounces of liquid and drink once daily, preferably with a meal
Take other medicines at least 2 hours before or after lactitol
Reduce the dose to 10 grams if stools become too loose
Tell your doctor if diarrhea is severe or constipation does not improve
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); keep tightly closed, protect from moisture
pearls: FDA-approved as Pizensy (lactitol) for chronic idiopathic constipation in adults
Osmotic sugar-alcohol laxative, structurally an analog of lactulose
Minimally absorbed - little systemic interaction or organ-based dose adjustment
Separate other oral drugs by at least 2 hours to avoid reduced absorption
Reduce dose to 10 g for persistent loose stools
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered on the same day. If it is nearly time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose and resume once-daily dosing. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Overdose is expected to cause diarrhea, abdominal cramping and possible dehydration with electrolyte loss. Treat with fluid and electrolyte replacement and supportive care; discontinue or reduce the dose.
